caption: The image depicts a woven textile sample composed primarily of two colors: a light beige or off-white and a medium brown. The weaving pattern forms various geometric shapes, including rectangles, squares, and grids, distributed in an organized, repetitive manner across the fabric. The textile is divided into several rectangular sections, each with its own dominant pattern, such as horizontal stripes, checkerboards, and vertical lines with interspersed squares. The left portion of the textile features alternating horizontal stripes in brown and beige, while the central and right portions are filled with intricate grid designs combining both colors, forming patterns reminiscent of both blocks and lines. The bottom edge of the textile is finished with a short fringe of untwisted beige threads. The background of the image is plain and neutral, focusing attention on the woven sample.
title: Woven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
